finding.claim: wipe() never enforces the OWNER role: requireRole() returns a boolean that is discarded, so any caller (including one with no roles) reaches repo.wipe(tenant).
finding.source: Any caller of Admin.wipe(User u, String tenant) via POST /tenants/{t}/wipe; u may hold any role set, including none.

trace.note: requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and never throws (documented at line 13)

finding.guards_checked: requireRole is non-throwing and its return value is not tested in wipe(); no other guard in wipe(). The sibling checkRole (lines 18-22) does throw and export() uses it, so the defect is specific to wipe().

verdict.guard_found: none. requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and never throws; its result is discarded as a bare statement at src/Admin.java:26, so wipe() proceeds to repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27. checkRole (lines 18-22) throws, but it is not called in wipe(). No other file in the repo (only src/Admin.java exists) provides an authorization filter before wipe().
verdict.reason: At src/Admin.java:26 the boolean from requireRole is discarded, so the OWNER check at line 14 never gates the unconditional repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27, and any authenticated caller who reaches wipe(), whatever roles they hold, can trigger the destructive operation.

finding.claim: Role checks in wipe() and export() are not tenant-scoped: User has no tenant binding and the tenant path parameter is never compared to the caller's tenant, so an OWNER of one tenant can wipe or export another tenant.
finding.source: tenant argument taken from the request path /tenants/{t}; caller's User(name, roles) with global role names only.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33 (data exfiltration); repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 (destruction)

trace.note: User record has only name and roles; no tenant field
export(User u, String tenant) entered with attacker-chosen tenant
checkRole(u, "OWNER") tests only the global role string, which passes for an OWNER of a different tenant
repo.export(tenant) runs for the foreign tenant

finding.guards_checked: checkRole/requireRole compare only the role name against u.roles(); neither method checks that u belongs to tenant. Upstream tenant binding could not be verified from this repo, so this is a candidate contingent on how roles are issued.

verdict.guard_found: Export: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) throws on a missing role, so it blocks callers with no OWNER role, but it never compares the tenant argument to the caller's tenant (User at src/Admin.java:4 has no tenant field). Wipe: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a bool and its result is discarded at src/Admin.java:26, so wipe() has no effective guard at all. No tenant-binding check exists in this repo; upstream enforcement could not be seen.
verdict.reason: Export at src/Admin.java:32-33 passes any caller whose global roles contain "OWNER" and then runs repo.export on the attacker-chosen tenant with no tenant comparison, and wipe at src/Admin.java:26-27 is worse because the requireRole result is discarded, so any caller can wipe any tenant. The candidate's description of wipe as a role check is inaccurate, but the cross-tenant conclusion holds within this file; the one caveat is that an upstream layer outside this repo could bind tenants, which I cannot see.
